questions: If there are no black cells in the initial grid, is an empty rectangle (i.e., choosing a > b or c > d) allowed, or must the final rectangle contain at least one cell?
Must the rectangle of black cells be contiguous in both dimensions, i.e., can the rectangle degenerate to a single row or a single column?
Are cells marked with '?' allowed to be painted either black or white arbitrarily, or are there any restrictions on how many of them can be painted black?

If the initial grid already contains black cells that are not aligned to form a single rectangle, is the answer always "No", or can we still paint some '?' cells to make the overall black region a rectangle that includes extra black cells?
In the case where multiple rectangles could satisfy the condition, does it matter which one is chosen, or is any valid rectangle sufficient?
Are the input strings guaranteed to contain only the characters '#', '.', and '?' with no whitespace or other symbols?
Should the output be exactly "Yes" and "No" with that capitalization, and without any extra whitespace or newline characters?
Are the row and column indices 1‑based as described, and does the rectangle definition include its boundary cells (i.e., cells with i = a or i = b, j = c or j = d) as black?
answers: No — the problem guarantees at least one black cell, so an all-white grid never occurs.

inline_prompts:
You are given a grid of H rows and W columns.
Let (i,j) denote the cell at row i (1 \leq i \leq H) from the top and column j (1 \leq j \leq W) from the left.
The state of the grid is represented by H strings S_1, S_2, \ldots, S_H, each of length W, as follows:
- If the j-th character of S_i is #, cell (i,j) is painted black.
- If the j-th character of S_i is ., cell (i,j) is painted white.
- If the j-th character of S_i is ?, cell (i,j) is not yet painted.
Takahashi wants to paint each not-yet-painted cell white or black so that all the black cells form a rectangle.
More precisely, he wants there to exist a quadruple of integers (a,b,c,d) (1 \leq a \leq b \leq H, 1 \leq c \leq d \leq W) such that:
For each cell (i,j) (1 \leq i \leq H, 1 \leq j \leq W),
if a \leq i \leq b and c \leq j \leq d, the cell is black;
otherwise, the cell is white.
Determine whether this is possible.
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
H W
S_1
S_2
\vdots
S_H
Output
If it is possible to paint all the not-yet-painted cells so that the black cells form a rectangle, print Yes; otherwise, print No.
Constraints
- 1 \leq H, W \leq 1000
- H and W are integers.
- Each S_i is a string of length W consisting of #, ., ?.
